text:
maria liu: Heads-up — forecasting run for Q4 promo window is back. Early signal shows rerank spikes + embeddings steady but longer tails. If we keep a single pooled strategy we risk latency SLO breaches during 1–3 hour spikes. Can we validate split-pool sims?

ajay singh: Agreed. I re-ran the sensitivity sims with updated traffic shape (heavy tail, 1% of minutes account for 25% of requests). Quick summary: realtime rerank needs consistent p95 < 200ms. Under mixed traffic model:
- Dedicated realtime pool (g5x2) @ 60 GPUs => ~18k qps-kernel capacity, p95 ~180ms
- Batch pool (spot/backfill) for large embedding/rerank jobs => sustains ~40k GPU-hours/day with flexible latency
Cost delta: mixed approach ~= +12% infra cost but reduces SLA risk by ~80%.

chen park: Can you share the sim command and config you used? I want to run with eu-west1 constraints (we've seen 20–30% lower effective throughput there due to networking).

ajay singh: Sure — here's the command I used:
```bash
./simulations/run_capacity.py --workload rerank+embeds --traffic-shape heavy-tail --realtime-gpus 60 --batch-gpus 120 --region-prefs us-west1,eu-west1 --kv-cache 0.6
```
Config notes: assumed KV cache hit 60% for rerank prefixes, batch jobs are pre-warmed with cached prefixes at 30% hit.

maria liu: Nice. For eu-west1 please lower effective throughput by 25% in the sim and add 12% network egress lag (we saw packet pacing during last firmware update).

ajay singh: Will do. Preliminary eu-west1-only numbers: to match the same p95 you need ~1.3x GPUs vs us-west1, and batch spillover to us-west1 needs to be allowed for 8–12 hours per day in peak scenarios.

noah: Important callout on storage I/O: our prefix cache warm-up for batch at scale increases S3 GET QPS; if batch and realtime share the same VPC egress path we could see transient saturation. We should model cache priming window and S3 throttle effects.

chen park: +1. Suggestion: dedicated egress route for realtime (smaller, pinned set), batch gets elastic NAT through burstable gateways. That keeps realtime deterministic.

ajay singh: Agreed. In sims I modeled 'egress-isolation' and saw p95 improvements of ~35ms at the cost of a couple of extra NICs and an additional load balancer. Cost vs SLA trade-off seems worth it for enterprise customers.

maria liu: Operational ask: can eng-infra run a full matrix of sims with these dims: realtime gpus [40,60,80], batch gpus [80,120,160], kv-cache hit [0.4,0.6,0.8], region penalty [0,0.25]? Output needed by EOD Wednesday so product can size Dedicated offers.

ops-bot: Simulation job queued: sim-run-183400a (ETA ~2h). Logs will be in /runs/1834001234-sim-run-183400a.log

noah: I'll add S3 GET rate and NAT egress counters to the sim metrics (will include 95/99 percentiles).

chen park: Also include a scenario where batch is throttled during business hours (08:00–20:00) so we can see spill patterns overnight vs daytime.

maria liu: Good — and add a simple cost model: spot vs reserved pricing for batch, and 3 commitment tiers for realtime. We need SKU-level rough numbers.

ajay singh: Will update sims and push CSVs to the shared drive. If anyone wants to tweak knobs, ping me and I'll fork the run.

sre_sam: Side note — check GPU preemption penalty in eu regions. Last month we saw ~6% additional lost work from preemptions during a similar stress test. That should be baked into the batch efficiency factor.

maria liu: Perfect. Thanks all. If the sims confirm the mixed-pool approach, product wants a short playbook (canary thresholds + autoscale ceilings + regional spillover rules). I'll draft after we get numbers. :thumbsup:
